Welcome to The Petersfield School. Our Academy has a long-established reputation for traditional values, high academic achievement and excellent student behaviour. Private Music Lessons
We offer private music lessons on a wide variety of instruments at TPS, please read the agreement linked below and sign up using the Book Now button.
SIGN UP FOR SEPTEMBER 2026 – JULY 2027
FAQ’s
Q: I don’t want my child to miss the same lesson each week – are music lessons always at the same time?
A: No. Lessons are timetabled on a rota, so your child will not miss the same lesson each week. #
We don’t have an instrument at home, is that an issue?
No! In the first instance please contact musiclessons@petersfieldschool.com and we can often help source an instrument.
How much are lessons?
Please look at the agreement for lessons as some prices do vary depending on group size and instrument learnt.
My child didn’t learn an instrument at primary school, is that an issue?
No! In fact we would encourage all students to be learning an instrument.
Do you offer any financial assistance with lessons?
Yes, please contact musiclessons@petersfieldschool.com for more information on this, and we will do our best to help, where possible.
My child wants to learn my that one instrument, is that possible?
Yes! We do advise thinking carefully about learning more than one instrument due to the amount of practice needed, however we would very much encourage it.

pageCache.pageTitle: Reporting to Parents - The Petersfield School The Petersfield School
pageCache.text:
Reporting to Parents
Attitude to Learning (ATL) grades, split into four key focus areas for each subject:
Application and Concentration
This represents a student’s ability to remain focused on a task or tasks for a length of time within lessons. This grade also reflects the amount of effort a student makes in class and at home.
Engagement
The degree to which a student is actively engaged in, and contributes to, lessons. This may be reflected by asking questions and contributing to discussions as well as displaying a willingness to seek out and take on extension tasks. The student will also show initiative and take responsibility for his/her own learning.
Ability to Meet Deadlines
This measures the extent to which classwork, homework and coursework is reliably completed and handed in on time; the quality of the work being commensurate with the student’s ability. It also reflects how organised the student is and how proficiently workload is managed e.g. how effectively the student is in planning and managing his/her time.
Being Prepared for Learning
Students consistently arrive to lessons punctually, correctly dressed and with the necessary items and equipment to allow them to take a full and active role within the lesson. Students are quick to settle and respond well to the prompts of the teacher.
Each category contains one of four grades based on a 1 – 4 scale:
1. Outstanding – Exceptional consistency demonstrated in this area
2. Good – Consistency demonstrated in this area
3. Inconsistent – Standards vary. This lack of consistency may adversely affect achievement
4. Unsatisfactory – Standards are often unacceptable. This may have a major impact on achievement

pageCache.pageTitle: Absence & Attendance - The Petersfield School The Petersfield School
pageCache.text:
Absence & Attendance
It is a legal requirement that your child attends school regularly. Excellent attendance is vital to students achieving their potential and, as a school, we place the highest importance on students being present and punctual. We expect students to achieve as close to 100% attendance as possible.
When your child is unwell you must inform the school, via ClassCharts, on the first morning of absence and, for safeguarding purposes, provide daily updates.
We ask that where possible you do not book routine medical appointments during the school day. Where this is not possible please ensure that your child attends school both before and /or after the appointment time as applicable.
For any planned absence you must submit a Leave of Absence Request Form in good time, please return it to the school reception or to Ms. Tavinor at stavinor@petersfieldschool.com
If you take your child on holiday, it will be recorded as unauthorised absence in all circumstances, and Penalty Notices will be issued in accordance with Hampshire County Council’s Code of Conduct.
Ten or more sessions of unauthorised absence in any 100-session period will result in a Penalty Notice.
Students should aim to arrive at school no later than 8.27 am (first bell), and they must be at their tutor room no later than 8.30 am (second bell). If your child is late they will receive a detention.
Attendance monitoring:
You will receive an attendance email at the end of each term, which will be colour-coded as follows;• Attendance levels less than 90% are awarded RED (persistent absentee)• Attendance levels of 90-95.99% are awarded AMBER (below target)• Attendance levels of 96-100% are given GREEN (meeting expectations)
Contact:Please do not hesitate to email our Attendance Officer, Ms. Tavinor at stavinor@petersfieldschool.com
Please refer to our Attendance Policy for more details.

pageCache.pageTitle: TPS celebrates record breaking GCSE success! - The Petersfield School The Petersfield School
pageCache.text:
TPS celebrates record breaking GCSE success!
Students at The Petersfield School, part of the high achieving Bohunt Education Trust (BET), are celebrating today after receiving their GCSE results, enabling them to embark confidently on the next stage of their education journey.
The 2025 cohort have achieved record-breaking results, whilst demonstrating great resilience, commitment and determination during their time at the school. Students have once again made outstanding progress, with over 84% achieving a grade 4 (grade C) or above in both English and maths, the highest achievement in the history of the school! Additionally, over a third of all the grades awarded at TPS today were at the top grade 7 to 9 (A*/A) level.
The accomplishments of students were celebrated across the board. Particular highlights include:
Several subjects secured truly remarkable results with over 85% of the students achieving grades 4 to 9 (A* to C) included English, maths, biology, chemistry, physics, geography, drama, dance, music, art, sociology, media and Mandarin.
This year’s results reflect The Petersfield School’s commitment to BET’s ethos of ‘enjoy, respect, achieve’, which underpins the culture and outcomes of all its schools. This includes delivering unparalleled educational opportunities and highly effective teaching to nurture and develop students into becoming “game-changers”.
Together, BET and The Petersfield School aim to support young people to flourish throughout their school journeys and then on into later life, with educational, enrichment and pastoral support both inside and outside the classroom.
Mark Marande, Headteacher at The Petersfield School, said:
“We are all exceptionally proud of our students and how hard they have worked at TPS to achieve such amazing, record breaking GCSE results. I would like to thank all our students, their families, our staff and the wider school community for their ongoing support for Team TPS. We cannot wait to see the great things that our students will accomplish in the next stage of their education and in the wider world.”
Neil Strowger, Trust Leader at BET, said:
“I am immensely proud of the efforts made by students across our schools. These GCSE results are testament to their hard work, dedication and resilience. Our commitment to ensuring the achievement of every student has led to these outcomes, which reflect the game-changing abilities of our students and staff and the excellence we strive for across BET.”

pageCache.pageTitle: Remote Learning - The Petersfield School The Petersfield School
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
Dear Parent/Guardian
At TPS we utilise multiple platforms to help support our students learning.
We use ClassCharts to help students keep track of their homework, as well as providing a way for staff to communicate with students and parents. As a result, it is incredibly important that students and parents are registered and able to access the ClassCharts platform. If you need any support with getting either yourself or your child onto ClassCharts then please don’t hesitate to ask your child’s tutor for a log in code.
We also utilise Showbie as our main learning platform. This enables students to access their lesson resources and communicate with their teachers. Resources are posted directly into the individual classes. Showbie enables digital feedback via written comments or voice notes, it also enables the use of video to back up lesson content. Teachers will always provide specific instructions with how to use the resources.
Important: If work is posted as an assignment in Showbie, this does not necessarily mean it is homework. Always check ClassCharts for assigned work.
Our online assessment platforms (eg Sparx, Seneca) are always available for use, and can be used to supplement any work provided if the need arises.
If you child is struggling to find any lesson resources, please do not hesitate to get in touch with the class teacher either directly by email. Any technical issues can also be directed to the IT Support team ( itsupport@petersfieldschool.com ).
Please see the links below for some further guidance and information on accessing resources on Showbie.
As always, can I take this opportunity to thank you for the work you are doing to support students home learning.
Mr J Morgan Leader of Digital Learning

Trips & Visits
Monday 29 June – Friday 3 July 2026
This year we are encapsulating our ethos of Enjoy, Respect, Achieve (ERA) with a week of fantastic enrichment opportunities for our students, in and outside of school, during ERA Week.
A variety of trips and events will be available to students, as part of the current curriculum or usual trip experiences we offer. Activities taking place in school focus on helping to create ‘Team TPS Game Changers’ and are either timetabled for the whole school or year specific participation, such as the Dance-a-thon for Year 7 through to Work Experience for Year 10. Accompanying all these great on-site events, several external school enrichment opportunities have been organised, ranging from GCSE day trips through to optional residential trips.
How do I sign my child up? Open the ERA Brochure linked below for more information on the experiences available and pay any required deposit via Parent Pay by Monday 23 February to secure a place.
The Brochure is being continually updated so we recommend you bookmark the link for ease of referral. Some trips may be added over the course of the year and prices can change over time. Any trips that have reach capacity will apply a waitlist, so please contact the Trip Leader should you like your child to be added.

Careers and Guidance
Careers and Guidance
Our Ethos
The Petersfield School is committed to providing students with high quality Information, Advice and Guidance regarding a full range of educational pathways and career options.
Sound careers guidance can support students in making informed decisions regarding their next steps. This includes, but is not limited to, option choices in Year 8, Post-16 plans, and higher education/post 18 choices. We support our students in this process by providing access to differentiated, impartial, and independent information and guidance about the range of options and opportunities most likely to help them achieve their ambitions.
We believe that giving students the best Careers education and guidance is vital to improving their motivation to learn and help them to achieve. We follow the Gatsby Benchmarks for Good Careers Guidance, including adhering to the Baker Clause of the Education Act.
All students at The Petersfield School are entitled to and able to access Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance that:
We are always looking for employers to come into school to help with Careers Fairs, Mock interview Day and inspire/motivate our students. If this is something you would like to help with, or find out any more information, please contact the Careers Team.

A former TPS student is living the dream in Hollywood after a film she produced won an Oscar for Best Short Film at the Academy Awards.
Luke recently won a BAFTA for a short film he worked on as first sound assistant and continues progressing in the film industry.
Felix C started Gymnastics at the age of 6 and made outstanding progress whilst a student at TPS.
I got first class teaching at TPS and some great opportunities and experiences in extra-curricular sport.
TPS always felt like a safe place to express myself and my hobbies without a fear of being told I wasn’t cool for playing with toys. Many teachers encouraged me to utilise LEGO in my work in Art, DT, even Maths and Geography!
From TPS I got the confidence and reassurance that you are able to achieve anything with the right attitude and enough hard work.
I started dancing at 3 and more seriously from the age of 12. I wanted to attend TPS because of their performing arts specialism, and they have given me so many opportunities to perform in dance and drama productions such as “Fame” at the New Theatre Royal Portsmouth and Rock Challenge at the Guildhall.

Good Schools Guide Review
Last term we were delighted to be selected for review in the Good Schools Guide. They select top state and independent schools with the purpose of providing parents with unbiased, candid reviews to enable them to make informed decisions when choosing a school for their child. Schools cannot pay to be included in the guide and you can find out more about how schools are selected and how the review process works on their website.
We are excited to share their full review of TPS and we believe that it really captures the very special nature of our school community.
The Petersfield School Review | The Good Schools Guide
“A truly outstanding school helping pupils to achieve their best through hard work, high aspirations and a culture where ‘opportunities to fly’ are part and parcel of the TPS experience. Pupils and parents are clear that ‘kids can have it all’ here.”
